speaker: Doctor
text: Given the large ovarian mass and significant ascites, I need to assess for Meigs' syndrome or malignancy. Do you have any history of hypertension or heart disease, and have you noticed any facial swelling or difficulty breathing when lying flat? REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CT scan is normal, this strongly suggests Meigs' syndrome rather than ovarian malignancy. Do you have a history of heart failure or liver disease, and have you noticed any shortness of breath that improves when sitting upright? REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal echocardiogram rules out cardiac causes for your shortness of breath and ascites, further supporting Meigs' syndrome. I need to confirm the nature of the mass, so please tell me if you have had any recent fevers or night sweats. REQUEST TEST: CA-125

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal CA-125, cardiac, and abdominal imaging, the evidence strongly points to Meigs' syndrome caused by a benign ovarian fibroma. I will request medical images of the ovarian mass to confirm its solid, fibrous nature. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming those details. The combination of a large ovarian mass, ascites, and shortness of breath with normal cardiac and oncologic markers is classic for Meigs' syndrome, likely caused by an ovarian fibroma. DIAGNOSIS READY: Meigs' syndrome secondary to ovarian fibroma
